name: 1701 Prairie Avenue — the William G. Hibbard house, Italianate, with its 1874 rear range (K01; refined by T-3240, T-3241, T-3242, T-1876)

function.note: The 1911 sheet labels the building with a 1911 use, '2½-storey brick dwelling over a stone basement (D, '2½SB'), with a 1-storey stone (blue) piece at its north-west corner and frame porches', which the draft does not carry back to 1904 (the T-1837 register warns not to assume the 1904 use from it). The register's family row, 'Italianate mansion with rear addition', names it a house, so the 1904 function is inferred residence on that row and the T-1840 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

built.note: The marker: 'William G. Hibbard Residence. Built 1869'.

research_note: T-3240 (piece 1 of T-1875) refines the district draft (T-2335) in place under the same id: the house is rebuilt from the K01 frontage assembly and its kits — K03 brick, K06 sash, K07 door and stoop, K08 canted bay, K10 bracketed cornice, K04 hip — instead of the draft builder. What is read: the 1911 Sanborn sheet 20 (the main block, the 1874 range behind it, the bay, the stone porch, the '2S.B.' strip and the open two-storey veranda drawn on its plan, '2½S.B.') through the T-1840 census; Chicagology's photograph of the front and south flank from the south-west (chicagology_1701_hibbard_photo), whose camera is solved in data/reference_views/; and the Glessner House Museum's rear photograph (glessner_blog_1701_hibbard_rear_photo). T-3241 (piece 2) adds the railed roof deck (k01_hip_deck), the lower south range (a K08 projection's range plan) and the corner porch's stone arcade (k01_porte_cochere's corner_porch), from the same photograph. Still to come: the two-level rear veranda and the rear range's oriel (T-3242); the carving, hoods and ironwork (T-1876). T-3255 adds the eared, crested window hoods of the front and the south flank and the corner and bay pilasters (k01_dressings). Liberty L-k01-hibbard-1701-3240.

documented_range.note: The house claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1840 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped); the photographs are undated (after the 1874 addition). Its building and loss dates are the per-building tickets' to read.

position.symbolic_location: 1701 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1701 (data/street_grid/1904.json), east side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 16th to 18th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 20).
position.note: The rear north corner of the main block's rectangle (the draft frame's u 17.5, v 1.2: lot frame u 41.5, v -10.3 from the middle of the rear lot line), read off the 1911 sheet's trace (s20fp-1701-b1) through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: its own fit residual, 3.08 m RMS on its control crossings, is all that is claimed. Rotation 179.61 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.

derivation.reason: The four derivation methods re-derive from the 1835 files; this position is re-derived from the traced sheet and the 1904 parcel by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py --check instead.

footprint.note: The main block read off the 1911 sheet's trace (s20fp-1701-b1 p1) in the draft's lot frame: its rear wall at u 17.5 (where the rear range and the open veranda meet it), the front at 30.0 (12.5 m deep), the north wall at v 1.2 and the line the sheet draws between the main block and the '2S.B.' strip on its south side at v 15.9 (14.7 m along the street). What stands outside it: the canted bay and the lower south range (bays), the 1874 rear range (rear_wings), the stone porch on the front's north part (corner_porch, T-3241; the recess behind it is not cut), and, still to be built, the two-level veranda (T-3242). The draft's rectangles r1-r4 are retired with it.

stories.note: '2½S.B.' printed on the 1911 sheet: two full storeys over a basement and a half storey in the roof; the photograph shows the two brick storeys over a stone basement whose lights stand above the fence.

construction.note: The 1911 sheet colours the building pink, brick; the photograph shows brick walls dressed in light stone (the quoin pilasters, the window hoods, the bay, the cornice) over a stone basement. T-3254: built as a brick house whose street front is K02 stone up to the principal floor and brick over it (stone_front.brick_above_m), the photograph's light basement under the brick.

stone_front.note: T-3254: the photograph's basement is smooth light stone from grade to a projecting water table at the principal floor (about 2.0 m, y 975-998 px at the bay through the solved camera, data/reference_views/hibbard_house_1701_prairie/chicagology_front.json), under the brick of the front, the bay and the south flank; the study register's word for the house is 'stone basement and belts'. Built as K02's smooth stone stopped at the principal floor (brick_above_m 2.0, T-1888) with two plinth courses to the basement lights' heads and a 0.3 m coping, and K01's belts kept across the brick. The print is monochrome and no source names the stone: the local Lemont limestone is RECONSTRUCTED (liberty L-k01-hibbard-1701-3254).

side_base.note: T-3254: the photograph carries the same light stone basement and its water table round the south-west corner and along the south flank (K01's high-v side wall here), the brick only over it. No picture shows the north flank, which stays brick to grade as the draft built it.

principal_floor_m.note: The stone basement's top stands about 2.0 m over grade through the photograph's solved camera (data/reference_views/hibbard_house_1701_prairie/chicagology_front.json), and its round-headed basement lights show over the fence: the principal floor is laid there. The camera's own height is set at a standing eye (1.6 m), so this figure carries that assumption (about ±0.3 m).

storey_heights_m.note: The bay's middle cornice, the second floor's mark on the front, stands about 6.3 m over grade and the main cornice's bed about 9.3-9.9 m through the photograph's solved camera (data/reference_views/hibbard_house_1701_prairie/chicagology_front.json): a principal storey of 4.3 m and an upper one of 3.7 m to a wall head at 10.0 m, the upper lights' round heads clear of the cornice's bed.

wall_thickness_front_m.note: RECONSTRUCTED: a two-brick wall under a mansion of this height; the sheet prints '12 12' against the rear range only.

service_wall_brick.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the K03 common brick panel the avenue's K01 houses wear; the monochrome photograph cannot give the brick's colour (it reads dark against the light stone dressings).

wall_head.note: The photograph's deep cornice on paired brackets all round the main block, painted light like the stone dressings; the K10 bracketed timber cornice laid in pairs. Its carving is T-1876's.

roof_form.note: A low hip over the main block: the photograph shows its slopes rising from the cornice on both faces it sees to a railed deck, which T-3241 builds (hip_deck): the hip is cut off level there.

roof_pitch_deg.note: The photograph's slopes rise short and steep from the cornice to the railed deck (hip_deck), through the solved camera (data/reference_views/hibbard_house_1701_prairie/chicagology_front.json): a 45 degree hip carries them from the eave to the deck's 13.3 m with the deck as wide as the rail reads, where the 35 degrees T-3240 laid to a ridge left a deck under 3 m across. The slopes are foreshortened and the camera is fitted below them, so the pitch is read to about 5 degrees.

eave_overhang_m.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the bracketed cornice's projection. T-3240 laid 0.75 m, as 1612's; under the 45 degree hip its soffit would drop onto the upper lights' heads, so it is 0.5 m (T-3241), still a deep cornice in the photograph's proportion.

stoop_width_m.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the K07 stoop's width. The stone porch (corner_porch, T-3241) stands beside the door, not round it; the door is reached by the kit's stoop.

entrance_bay.note: The photograph's tall dark arch between the corner porch and the bay, at about v 5.8-8.3 through the photograph's solved camera (data/reference_views/hibbard_house_1701_prairie/chicagology_front.json): the entrance, in the middle of the front's three bays.

front_bays.note: Three bays along the front, north to south in this frame (v 0 at the north wall): the north bay behind the corner porch the 1911 sheet draws in stone ('1', blue, v about 0.3-5.7), its upper light read at about v 6.7 through the photograph's solved camera (data/reference_views/hibbard_house_1701_prairie/chicagology_front.json) over the entrance at 7.0, and the two-storey bay at 10.4. The sheet draws the bay over v 8.3-11.0, the photograph over about 9.1-13.7; it is laid between them (see bays).

side_bays.note: RECONSTRUCTED: three windows a storey in the north wall, facing 1637's side yard. No picture shows the north side.

north_bays.note: The south wall's lights, s from the front corner, read through the photograph's solved camera (data/reference_views/hibbard_house_1701_prairie/chicagology_front.json): over the lower south range, a single round-headed light at s 3.9 and a pair at 5.55 and 6.75, sills about 6.75 m; toward the rear a pair at 9.9 and 11.15 on both storeys, sills about 2.6 and 6.75 m. The lower south range (bays, T-3241) stands before the principal storey from s 1.1 to 4.0, so the light T-3240 reconstructed at s 3.9 is gone; the one at 6.15, past the range, is reconstructed as the pair's spacing above.

rear_bays.note: RECONSTRUCTED: three windows a storey in the rear wall south of the 1874 range, s from the south end; the two-level veranda the rear photograph shows standing against the south part of this wall stands before them (rear_veranda, T-3242).

sash_by_storey.note: Read through the photograph's solved camera (data/reference_views/hibbard_house_1701_prairie/chicagology_front.json): the principal storey's lights about 2.55 m tall over sills 0.6 m above the floor, the upper storey's about 2.15 m; taller than the contract's starting range, which a light read off a picture may be.

basement_lights.note: The photograph's basement lights over the fence, in the stone base under the principal storey; their heads and size are the kit's area light.

roof_covering.note: RECONSTRUCTED: painted standing-seam tin on the low hip; the photograph's slopes read plain and light.

chimneys.note: The photograph's tall stack rising through the roof's south half, a corbelled cap; a second over the north rooms, as the rear photograph shows two stacks over the main block. Their places are read loosely (the roof is foreshortened). The stacks' tops stand 2.8 m over the deck (T-3241: the hip now stops at its deck), the tall south stack running out of the photograph's top edge, at least 16 m up.

rainwater.note: RECONSTRUCTED: half-round copper gutters behind the cornice, round downpipes on the rear wall and the north wall between their lights, clear of the corners' paired brackets and of the street front the photograph shows without one.

window_kit.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the K06 two-over-two sash in every light, the round-headed ones under the kit's round head, and its area light in the basement without a well; the photograph's basement lights stand over grade.

street_front_round_heads.note: The photograph's lights on the front are round-headed on both storeys, each under a light stone hood; built as K01's round heads, dressed by eared_round_heads (T-3255), whose crest stands where the kit's key block stood.

eared_round_heads.note: T-3255 (piece 2 of T-1876): every round-headed light of the front and of the south flank (K01's north wall) stands under a light stone hood in the photograph: a broad band round the arch whose feet step out into ears at the springing and hang down the jambs, and a pointed crest standing up off its crown. Read through the solved camera (data/reference_views/hibbard_house_1701_prairie/chicagology_front.json) against the lights the record already sizes: the band about a fifth of a metre broad, the ears about 0.12 m past it and 0.3 m down, the crest about 0.3 m wide rising 0.25 m over the band. The pair toward the rear on the flank meet ear to ear between them, as the photograph's do. The carving on the band and the crest is drawn as plain stone (liberty L-k01-hibbard-1701-3255).

corner_pilasters.note: T-3255: the photograph's tall light stone pilaster on the corner of the front and the south flank, from the stone basement's top to a carved capital under the cornice's frieze (its bed at 9.45 m, K10's 0.55 m frieze under the 10.0 m eave), about 0.45 m broad on each face through the solved camera. Built as a corner pilaster wrapped round both faces: a base, a plain shaft and a two-stage capital; the shaft's carved bands and the capital's leaves are drawn as plain stone (liberty L-k01-hibbard-1701-3255). The front's north corner stands behind the corner porch and the flank's rear corner reads plain brick in the photograph; neither is dressed.

entrance_kit.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the K07 panelled door at the head of a straight stoop from the walk, the front wall 7.74 m from the lot's street line (the sheet's lot, u 20.24). The photograph's entrance stands in a tall round arch beside the stone porch (T-3241 builds the porch); K07's round-arched door is laid only in a K02 stone front's courses, so this brick front keeps the panelled door under a flat head.

windows.why_not_ordinary: the photograph's paired lights in the bay's face, narrower than the wall's sash so two stand in its 2.5 m face
the paired upper lights over them, the same pair
the photograph's narrow round-headed light in the lower south range's south face, narrower than the wall's sash
an oriel's cheek light: narrower than an ordinary sash so it fits the canted cheek
the rear photograph's pair of round-headed lights in the oriel's front, narrower than the range's sash so two stand in its 2.6 m face

bays.note: The photograph's two-storey bay in light stone on the front's south part, canted, two round-headed lights a storey in its face under a cornice at the second floor and another under the main cornice. The sheet draws a canted bay over v 8.3-11.0 (the K01 frame), 1.3 m out; through the photograph's solved camera (data/reference_views/hibbard_house_1701_prairie/chicagology_front.json) its junctions read about v 9.1 and 13.7. Laid at 10.4, 3.6 m at the wall and 1.2 m out (K08 holds a canted bay to 1.2 m): within both readings' spread, and the difference is written in the match record. The lower south range (lower_south_range, T-3241): the photograph's one-storey brick block on the south flank, read through its solved camera (data/reference_views/hibbard_house_1701_prairie/chicagology_front.json): set back about 1.1 m from the front corner, 2.9 m along the flank and 3.1 m out from it, its walls to a moulded cornice about 5.2-5.7 m up and a low pierced parapet over it to about 6.1 m, a round-headed light in its west face and a narrower one in its south face. Built as a K08 projection's `range` plan. The 1911 sheet draws a strip only about 1.6 m wide on this side ('2S.B.'); the photograph is followed and the difference is liberty L-k01-hibbard-1701-3241. The parapet's pierced slots are drawn as the kit's stone balustrade. The range's oriel (range_oriel, T-3242): the rear photograph's corbelled oriel on the 1874 range's south face at the upper storey, read through its solved camera (data/reference_views/hibbard_house_1701_prairie/ghm_rear.json): its front about u -12.1 to -15.2 and 0.8 m out, its east cheek meeting the wall at about -15.4, its floor at the range's second floor (6.3 m) on carved brackets reaching down to about 4.6 m, its top under the range's cornice, a pair of round-headed lights in its front and one in its cheek (drawn square-headed). Built as a K08 canted oriel on the wing's wall, s 13.65 from the main block; its stone, its 0.45 m cants, its seven corbel courses for the photograph's brackets and its low hip for the carved cresting are reconstructed (liberty L-k01-hibbard-1701-3242). T-3254: the lower south range stands on the house's stone basement, its plinth carried up to the water table at the principal floor (plinth_m 2.0), as the photograph shows it, brick only over it. T-3255: the bay's four angles (its two junctions with the front and the two corners of its face) are carved stone pilasters from the stone basement's top, one a storey under a capital, as the photograph's light shafts stand at them (K08's pilasters, T-2931); their carving is the kit's plain shaft.

rear_wings.note: The 1874 rear range the 1911 sheet traces behind the main block's north half (s20fp-1701-b1, draft frame u about -0.2 to 17.5, v -0.4 to 8.0; here u -17.7 to 0, v 0 to 6.8). The sheet draws its north wall about 1.2-1.6 m north of the main block's; it is built in the main block's north wall line, because K10's cornice cannot yet turn the main block's rear corner inside a wing that buries it (liberty L-k01-hibbard-1701-3240; no picture shows the north side). The rear photograph shows it in brick, as tall as the main block's wall head, its lights round-headed. Its windows' places are reconstructed (the picture is small and oblique), except the south face's (the wing's north wall in this frame), which T-3242 moved to the three lights the photograph's lower storey shows at s 2.6, 7.2 and 10.0, none under the oriel; the upper storey keeps the light at 7.2 the photograph does not show there, since a wing cuts one list of lights through every storey. Its corbelled oriel stands on that face (bays, range_oriel, T-3242); its heavy bracketed cornice is still built as a flat deck's fascia.

boundary.note: The photograph's iron fence on a stone curb along the street line before the house (0.24 m inside the lot's line, as 1726's coping stands), with a gate at the walk. T-3254: its panels are a lattice of interlaced round arches, their crossings making rows of pointed loops the full height between the rails (x 560-1600 px, about 17 px a loop at some 22 m, so about 0.2 m, the distance read to perhaps a quarter), built as K11's lattice of interlaced arches (1620's, T-2406) on a 0.25 m bay, each arch two bays wide: the reading's upper end, which keeps the fence's iron to about two thirds of a 0.2 m bay's in a scene already over its desktop memory ceiling (T-3173). The cast pattern's exact profile is the kit's.

yard.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the K14 walk in flags from the stoop's foot to the gate, its width and wear the kit's.

corner_porch.note: The corner porch on the front's north end: the 1911 sheet's stone piece ('1', blue; trace s20fp-1701-b1 p2), 5.46 m along the front from the north wall and 1.24 m before the front's line, and Chicagology's photograph, read through its solved camera (data/reference_views/hibbard_house_1701_prairie/chicagology_front.json): a one-storey stone arcade on the principal floor's stone podium (its floor about 2.0 m up), a narrow arched opening at v about 0.9-2.6 and a wide one at about 2.8-5.0 on its front with a sash seen through each, a narrow arch in its south return, the arches springing about 4.35-4.75 m up and crowning about 5.2-5.5 m, an entablature about 5.65-6.3 m and a low balustrade over it to about 6.7 m. Built by k01_porte_cochere's corner_porch (T-3241). The photograph's slender columns and carved capitals are drawn as plain piers, its entablature's brackets and its balusters' turning are the kit's, and the sheet's porch runs back 1.85 m behind the front's line where the front is recessed; K01 lays the main block as a rectangle, so the wall behind the arcade stands in the front's line (liberty L-k01-hibbard-1701-3241).

hip_deck.note: The photograph's railed deck over the hip, read through its solved camera (data/reference_views/hibbard_house_1701_prairie/chicagology_front.json): the slopes rise from the cornice to a level deck whose pale rail, pierced with a row of round holes between posts, stands about 13.3-14.1 m over grade; the rear photograph shows the same rail over the rear. Built by k01_hip_deck (T-3241): K05's hip cut off level at 13.3 m and a rail 0.8 m high round the deck's edge. The camera was fitted on the walls below 9.5 m, so the deck's height and place are read to about 0.5 m; the rail's section, its holes' 0.36 m size and 0.5 m pitch and its posts' 2.4 m spacing are reconstructed (liberty L-k01-hibbard-1701-3241).

rear_veranda.note: The rear photograph's open veranda of two decks against the main block's rear wall south of the 1874 range, read through its solved camera (data/reference_views/hibbard_house_1701_prairie/ghm_rear.json): its run along the wall from about 1.1 m clear of the range to the main block's south corner (v 7.9-14.7) and about 2.6 m out; the lower deck about 1.7-2.0 m over grade, built a step under the principal floor at 1.85; the upper an open balcony about 5.1-5.5 m up, built at 5.2, its rail's top under the upper storey's sills as the photograph shows; five stations of paired posts along the front; a band of spindles under the upper deck; a balustrade round both decks; and a flight of steps down off the lower deck's front in its north bay. Built by k01_rear_veranda (T-3242). The posts' and rails' sections, the square balusters for the photograph's turned ones, the stations' even spacing, the flight's width, treads and stone, and the light paint (the photograph is monochrome) are reconstructed; the posts are carried to grade where the photograph's planting hides what stands under the lower deck. The camera reads the main block about 2 m wider than its footprint, so the photograph's veranda runs on south past the model's corner (liberty L-k01-hibbard-1701-3242).
